content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work studies how to efficiently and effectively leverage and ensemble heterogeneous views. The proposals are shared encoding for each view, and a contrastive loss across encoded views. Authors demonstrate their proposals through experiments on MS-COCO and Flickr30K.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. Writtings are clear in general.
2. Extensive experiments are conducted to validate the proposals.

Weaknesses
1. The main idea of ensembling augmented views is not insightful. And I have to say the technical contribution is marginal, since lots of existing works have explored model ensembling (for example [A]). At most time, a simple model ensembling acts as the engineering trick widely adopted in captioning challenges, rather than a scientific problem in this field. Moreover, the difference against existing attention-based model ensembling might be the contrastive Loss, which is a simple migration from MoCo.
[A] Multi-modal Feature Fusion with Feature Attention for VATEX Captioning Challenge 2020.
2. In Table 1, it is better to upgrade each baseline with mode ensembling for fair comparison.
3. In Table 3, I am curious to see more results with SCST training for each run, which better aign with the final performances in Table 1.
4. Different trade-off parameters of contrastive Loss are set in cross-entropy training and SCST training. So is the performance sensitive to the choice of this hyperparameter?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The main idea is clear. But the technical contribution is marginal.
content.summary_of_the_review: My main concerns lie in the limited technical contribution and insufficient experimental results. Please check the details in Weaknesses.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an image captioning model, termed HEAV, where four views of images are employed: detected object features, visual features extracted by CLIP, image grid features and retrieved textual descriptions using CLIP. The model itself is not novel since some existing works have explored image-text pre-training for image captioning, such as Oscar. The advantage of the paper is that the performance of the proposed model is better than existing models and it is data-efficient. Nevertheless, this paper shows that introducing more information is able to improve the quality of the generated captions.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

S1: The proposed model performs very well,  outperforming existing models that employ large-scale pre-training.

S2: The proposed model is data-efficient, i.e., using a small-scale dataset to train, it also outperforms its counterparts.

Weaknesses:

W1: The novelty and motivation of the proposed model need to be discussed since there are many works that employ multiple views of the input images to enhance image captioning.

W2: It is not surprising that the performance of the proposed model is better than existing works since it employs more information and modules, such as object detection, CLIP, grid image features, and text features. Plus, there is no ablation study on the views, so it is not clear which view is more important for image captioning.

W3: There is one view -- textual descriptions retrieved by CLIP, but details are missing. For example, how many retrieved texts are used? Does the number of retrieved texts matters? What are the candidate texts for CLIP retrieval?

W4: Eq. (4) is incorrect. Why is the rightmost part an approximation of the leftmost part?

W5: Only using CIDEr, SPICE is not enough to reflect the quality of the generated captions, some metrics on distinctiveness should be considered, for example, CIDErBtw [1,2].

[1] J. Wang et al. Compare and reweight: Distinctive image captioning using similar image sets. ECCV, 2020.

[2] J. Wang et al. On Distinctive Image Captioning via Comparing and Reweighting. TPAMI, 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The method is clear, but some details of the experiments are missing, such as how many retrieved texts are used. The novelty and motivation of the proposed model need to be discussed. We may reproduce the proposed approach if more details are given.
content.summary_of_the_review: Though the proposed model outperforms existing works, some details should be provided and the novelty should be discussed.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
As pre-trained models have made great progress in the study of image encoding, visual encoding in Video captioning (e.g. using grid features, object detection, text encoding) has also made great progress. This variety of encoding approaches raises the question of how to efficiently and effectively combine these heterogeneous set of encodings. The article proposes to consider these encoding approaches as augmented views of the input image, encode each view independently with a shared encoder and provide a hierarchical decoder then adaptively ensembles the encoded views according to their usefulness by first ensembling within each view at the token level, and then across views at the view level.
This method demonstrates significant performance improvements of +5.6% CIDEr on MS-COCO compared to state of the art under the same trained-from-scratch setting and +16.8% CIDEr on Flickr30K with semi-supervised training.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
1.	The hierarchical structure of the paper proposed ensembles the encoded views by adaptively weighing the views according to their usefulness.
2.	The views are regarded as the augmentations of the input image and are separately encoded by a shared transformer encoder, which reduces the computation complexity of the Transformer architecture.
3.	The method of this paper incorporates a contrastive loss, and its formulation does not require annotated pairs and can work with unlabelled image-only data to achieve better performance.
Weaknesses:
1.	The shared encoder can only make ensembling of different visual encodings through training, and cannot learn additional features by using backpropagation of losses obtained from video captioning training due to the frozen pre-trained models.
2.	Contrastive loss which incorporated in learning representation is done by randomly zeroed-out tokens, and it looks like rather generated learning than contrastive learning in semi-supervised learning.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The overall structure of the article is relatively clear and the content is novel in several aspects, proposing the encoding of different pre-trained models as data augmentation of samples to better accomplish visual language tasks through a hierarchical architecture, but the narrative of the contrastive learning part is not clear enough, without formulas and detailed descriptions, which may be problematic in terms of concrete implementation.
content.summary_of_the_review: The article presents several novel ideas, treating different visual encodings as data augmentation of the same sample, and designing a hierarchical model to improve accuracy. However, the description of the part of contrastive learning is not accurate and specific enough, lacking the corresponding formula and the reason for adoption, and there are references that do not conform to the relevant content.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The author uses multiple pretrain-model to generate multiple image features for image captioning task. The author proposes a low-computation and effective method to leverage the multiple features. On two image caption dataset, the model achieves the state-of-the-art result.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. HEAV designs a low-parameter method to leverage the multiple views from multiple image encodings. The shared transformer structure is illuminating. HEAV also designs a reasonable decoder stage to ensemble the multiple image views.
2. The performance on COCO and Filter300K is convincing and the ablation studies are abundant.

Weakness
1. The motivation of HEAV, leveraging different visual features from different image encoders, seems incremental.
2. The experiments shows obvious performance improvements on CIDer metric, while the performance change is little on other metrics.
3. The ablation study lacks further discussion from feature angels to analyze why multiple encoder improves the image caption task
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The ablation study lacks further discussion from feature angels to analyze why multiple encoder improves the image caption task
2. The novelty is incremental.
content.summary_of_the_review:
1. Does the ensemble strategy work effectively on other multimodality tasks including VQA and Visual retrieval?
2. From feature point of view, why does multiple encoders help generating the captions?
3. What's the difference between CIDer metric and other metrics? Why HEAV improve significantly on CIDer but has little improvement on other metric ?
